title: Existing short-word completion transport is invertible
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], a family of schemes $W_a$ on small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the recorded actual system operations and section-normalized ringed models [def-sf-integral-system-operations, def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge]. Let $B$ be a typed word in variables, coefficient units, tensor, separated finite-type quasi-compact pullback, proper direct image, and quasi-compact open extension, with at most three operation vertices. Its canonical completion transport is recursively identity on variables and units, tensor of child transports followed by the specified quotient-completion tensor unit, pullback of the child transport followed by the specified pullback completion unit, the right-adjoint realization transport on proper direct image, and open extension of the child transport. Let the integral inputs be finite-Tor constructible with normalized reductions and compatible etale origins, with all word systems normalized and satisfying common finite cohomological and Tor bounds [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain]. Then this canonical transport from the ordinary ringed evaluation of $B$ to its completed evaluation is an isomorphism. This is exactly the already-published completionMap_isIso helper, independently of generator coherence.

proof.text: Induct on the word. Variables and units have identity completion transport. The shortWordIntegralDomain theorem puts each child of a tensor, pullback or proper-image vertex in the finite-Tor constructible domain (or identifies it with the scalar unit). primitiveCompletionEffectivity makes the specified tensor and pullback completion units and the reconstruction unit invertible there. Tensor and unary functors preserve the child isomorphisms. Proper image uses its fixed right-adjoint-conjugate realization; open extension applies its exact functor to the child isomorphism. This is exactly the current complete proof of completionMap_isIso.
